# What is in the library

<!-- Written by `npm run extract`: do not edit. -->

Everything the games have made, by what it is. Import any of it as
`madness-engine/<path>` (without the `.js`). Where games made different
versions of one thing, the default is the one most games have, and each
other is beside it, named after the oldest game that has it.

## characters

The people, creatures and monsters. Most are sculpted definitions (the default export) for `createModel`; `humanoid`, `quadruped`, `person` and `wardrobe` are the bodies and clothes they are built from; `slime`, `egg` and `boulder` are built from their own geometry.

## props

What lies about to be picked up: sculpted, still, for `createStatic`, and the colourable roleplaying dice (`DICE`) in `props/dice`.

| Path | Versions (games) | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `props/bucket` | `bucket` (rocknroller-ii) | A bucket of popcorn from the concession stand: a tall paper tub in red and white stripes, wider at the top, its rim rolled over, a yellow oval on the front with POPCORN across it in red; and the popcorn heaped up over the rim, a few pieces fallen onto it. |
| `props/case` | `case` (rocknroller) | A road case: black textured laminate in an aluminium frame, an angle down every edge and a chrome ball corner over every corner, the lid's joint running round it in a bright extrusion; two butterfly latches on the front, a recessed handle in each end; PICKS stencilled on the front in white, FRAGILE in red on the lid, and a strip of gaffer tape with BACKLINE written on it in marker. |
| `props/chest` | `chest` (dungeon-roller) | A treasure chest: oak planks with the grain in them, a barrel-vaulted lid of staves, two iron bands over it all studded with rivets, an iron bracket on every corner, strap hinges at the back, a ring handle on each end, and on the front a gold lock plate with a keyhole and the hasp coming down over it. |
| `props/clapper` | `clapper` (rocknroller-ii) | A clapperboard: a black slate ruled in white — PROD at the top, ROLL, SCENE and TAKE across the middle with their numbers chalked in, DIRECTOR and CAMERA under — and TAKE 2 chalked big on the back; the clapsticks along its top, striped black and white on the slant, the upper one swung open on a steel hinge. |
| `props/demo` | `demo` (metroll) | A demo tape: a cassette in a dark shell, its two halves screwed together at the corners and the foot, a paper label on each side — the side's letter in a box, a red band, DEMO in marker and the band's name crossed out and written again under it — and a window through it all where the two hubs sit with the tape wound on them, more on one than the other. |
| `props/globe` | `globe` (rocknroller-iii) | A snow globe: a souvenir, three hide at every stop. |
| `props/gold` | `gold` (dungeon-roller) | A heap of gold: coins piled up in a mound, two stacks of them beside it, more slid off onto the floor, each coin a proper coin — a raised rim, a milled edge and a star struck in the middle of it — and three cut gems in amongst them: a ruby, an emerald and a sapphire, faceted, the light coming through them. |
| `props/key` | `key` (dungeon-roller) | A key: big, old and gold. |
| `props/lighter` | `lighter` (rocknroller, rocknroller-iii, metroll) | A lighter, held up and lit: the cheap disposable kind every pocket at the gig has one of. |
| `props/pass` | `pass` (metroll, rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii, rocknroller) | A backstage pass: a laminated card on a lanyard. |
| `props/pick` | `pick` (rocknroller, rocknroller-iii, metroll) | A pile of guitar picks: nine of them, slid into a heap, in the colours and the stuff picks come in — tortoiseshell, pearloid, plain celluloid in pink and blue and yellow and white — each the proper shape, a rounded triangle with a firm point, thin as a fingernail, some with a gold star or a ring printed on. |
| `props/popcorn` | `popcorn` (rocknroller-ii) | A handful of popcorn, spilled from somebody's bucket: popped kernels in a heap, each one burst into four to six crinkled white wings round a little core, a scrap of the golden hull still stuck to it, a yellow blush of butter toward the hull. |
| `props/potion` | `potion` (dungeon-roller) | A healing potion: a round flask of clear glass (the marble's glass) with the red draught glowing in it two thirds full, a few bubbles risen to the top of it; a cork pushed into the neck; a cord wound twice round the neck under the lip and knotted, its two ends hanging down over the shoulder, and on the longer one a paper tag with a red cross on it. |
| `props/record` | `record` (rocknroller) | A gold record: a disc of gold-plated vinyl, the grooves running round it in fine rings with the gaps between the songs showing, a rolled bead at its rim and a smooth run-out round the label; the label red, GOLD across it and SIDE A under that, the spindle hole through the middle. |

| `props/halloween` | `halloween` (blubber) | October's scenery: hay bales, dead trees, a scarecrow, gravestones and stone crosses, an obelisk, coffins, heaps of bones, glowing toadstools and the witch's cauldron. |
| `props/groceries` | `groceries` (bodega) | A corner store's stock: a pile of Gala apples, a hand of bananas, a truss of tomatoes, a head of lettuce, russet potatoes, navel oranges, a bunch of carrots, yellow onions, bell peppers, green grapes; a gable milk carton, a yogurt tub, wrapped cheddar, butter, an open carton of brown eggs, film-wrapped chicken and beef trays, deli turkey, orange juice, bacon, sour cream; a twist-tied loaf of bread; rice, spaghetti in a box with a window, cereal, a can of black beans, ground coffee, flour, sugar, oats, peanut butter; a bag of chips, a box of cookies, a candy bar; a 2 L cola and a 1 L water; a frozen pizza and a tub of vanilla ice cream; and the shipping carton it all arrives in. `GROCERIES` has them by name. |
| `props/cafe` | `cafe` (venture-cafe) | A breakfast café's furniture in one palette of walnut, green cushion and brass: the dining chair (`cafechair`, a seat 0.14 up like the plain `chair`, a slatted back with brass-capped posts), the pedestal table (`cafetable`), the counter stool (`cafestool`) and the booth (`cafebooth`, a long bench with a high back and a table in front of it). `CAFE` has them by name. |
| `props/harvest` | `harvest` (blubber) | November's: the harvest lantern — a white pumpkin with rings of holes punched through it and a candle inside (`gourd`; dark, `whitepumpkin`) — corn shocks, barrels, a haystack with a pitchfork in it, and the feast table. |
| `props/pumpkin` | `pumpkin` (blubber) | Pumpkins: a fat one of eight ribs, squat, its crown sunk round a crooked stalk, waxy orange deepening into the grooves. |
| `props/sweets` | `sweets` (blubber) | The sweets, from October to December. |
| `props/winter` | `winter` (blubber) | December's: the snow lantern — a cone of snowballs heaped in rings with a candle inside, glowing out between them (`snowlantern`; unlit, `snowheap`) — the big snowball that rolls down the halls, snowy pines, rocks under snow, and clusters of ice crystals. |
| `props/dice` | `DICE` (engine) | Eight standalone dice props: D4 (a numeral at each corner, read at the top vertex), numbered and pip D6, D8, D10, percentile D% (the same ten-sided shape as D10, numbered 00–90 with each numeral pointing toward its nearest tip), D12 and D20. Resin, number/pip ink and the D20's highlighted 20 can be coloured independently. |
| `props/book` | (engine) | The Book of Madness: a hardcover whose cover is one welded piece (back board, hinge groove, spine, hinge groove, front board) bent every frame from its rest shape by a curvature field, the way Slimey's orb is deformed from its `base`, with leaves rooted in the spine that curl through the gutter as they turn. Leather, foil emblem (pentagram, eye, kraken, moon, skull), trim, title, endpapers and every page are painted, and the words are the caller's: `pages` (a list or a function), `setPages()`, or `setText(longString)`, which paginates real text by measuring it (`print: true` for a plain face). `createBook(GFX, { title, pageCount, cloth, foil, emblem, trim, paper, pages })` gives `pose()`, `open()`, `close()`, `next()`, `prev()`, `setStyle()` and `update(dt)`. `coverDetail` ('full' or 'low': a small cover, without the relief, for a book seen from afar) and `setCoverDetail(detail)` let a scene paint covers in full only near the camera. |
| `props/bookcase` | (engine) | An empty bookcase of boards, for models: `compartments` says where each shelf's space is; `place(model, { compartment, x, z })` puts anything on one, `standBook(book)` stands a real Book model (props/book.js) spine out, `shelve(books, { spread })` stands a list of them along the shelves, `clear()` takes them off, and `stockBooks(n)` makes options for a varied stock (light books for a shelf: a small picture, pages written only when opened). The wood is the library's (`textures/wood`) when that file is present, plain painted boards when it is not, picked up with no change when it arrives (`WOOD_SOURCE` says which). `createBookcase(GFX, { species, finish, shelves, width, height, depth, books })`. |
| `props/wood-table` | (engine) | A customizable set of wood tables built like the bookcase (same species, finishes and `textures/wood` grain, plain boards when that is absent): `kind` (dining, coffee, side, console, desk, bar) picks starting measures, and `shape` (rectangle, round, oval), `legs` (square, tapered, turned, trestle), `apron`, `shelf`, `drawer`, `width`, `depth`, `height`, `species`, `finish` change them. `surface` and `lowerShelf` say where things stand; `place(model, { x, z, turn, onShelf })` stands one there and `clear()` removes them. `createWoodTable(GFX, options)`; `createTableSet(GFX)` lines up one of each kind. |
| `props/tile-kitchen` | (engine) | A bistro kitchen's counter and wall, ported from Short Order: a slab of honed Calacatta marble with its top on `y = 0`, and behind it at `z = 0` a wall of bottle-green glazed subway tile with a brass rail on standoffs and a brass quarter-round where tile meets stone. For something to stand on and be shot against. `createTileKitchen(GFX, { width, depth, height, railHeight, marbleSize, scale })` gives `{ group, counter, wall, rail }`. |
| `props/wood-chair` | (engine) | A customizable set of wooden chairs built like the wood tables (same species, finishes and `textures/wood` grain): `kind` (dining, spindle, ladder, armchair, stool, barstool, windsor) picks a starting chair, and `seat` (square, round, saddle), `legs` (square, tapered, turned), `back` (slat, spindle, ladder, bow, none), `splay` (degrees the legs stand out, with turned stretchers), `rake` and `spindles` (for a bow back: its lean and its number of arrow spindles), `curve` (metres the back bows out behind the sitter, 0 flat), `arch` (metres the middle of the back rises above its ends: an arched top rail, the slats and spindles following it), `arms`, `stretchers`, `width`, `depth`, `height`, `backHeight`, `species`, `finish` change it. Every part overlaps what it joins, so a chair is one piece. `seatSurface` says where to sit and `place(model)` sits one there. `createWoodChair(GFX, options)`; `createChairSet(GFX)` lines up one of each kind. |
| `props/track-light` | (engine) | Track lighting: a ceiling rail with the light show's PAR cans hung from it on stems, each turned to aim where it is told. `length`, `cans` (spaced evenly), `drop`, `finish` (black, bronze, white), `color`; `light` (one shared warm point light, since the renderer has eight at most), `intensity`, `reach`, `decay`, `lightAt`. `aim(point)` and `aimCan(index, point)` aim in the track's coordinates, `aimAt(worldPoint)` once it is placed. `createTrackLight(GFX, options)`. |
| `props/glass-entry` | (engine) | A glass storefront entryway: a pair of glass doors with long pulls, side lights and a transom in a `frame` (bronze, black, white), daylight beyond the glass (`outside`), and a `mat` just inside. `width`, `height`, `doorWidth`, `doorHeight`. Faces +z; `doorway` says where to walk through. `createGlassEntry(GFX, options)`. |
| `props/bowling-ball` | `createBowlingBall` (engine) | A high-resolution glossy resin bowling ball with three true recessed finger wells and five seamless surface designs (marble, spiral, flame, split and blotch). Colors and designs are changeable at runtime. |
| `props/putter` | `createPutter` (engine) | A customizable putter at real size: blade, mallet and half-moon heads with a face insert and a (glowing) sight line, a wrapped leather grip with a metal cap at each end, and the shared metals for the head, shaft and fittings, all changeable at runtime. Built butt-down like the swords, with `playRotation` and `sole` for laying the head on the floor. |
| `props/glassglobe` | `glassglobe` | A clear glass Earth: the continents etched on it as frosted glass from real coastline coordinates (`textures/earth/map`, Natural Earth 1:50m land and big lakes), near side and far side as on a real etched globe, with room inside for Krystal's mist and a colorized map of anything over the Earth (`createGlassGlobe(GFX, { radius })`; `orient(lat, lon)`, `setField(canvas)`, `setMist(settings)`, `update(dt)`). |
| `props/glass-planets` | `GLASS_PLANETS`, `createGlassPlanet`, `loadGlassPlanetMaps` (engine) | The planets in glass, each with its own mist: `earth`, `mars`, `moon`, `jupiter` (its clouds as a colored field) and `jupiter-etched` (its zones etched in the glass). `createGlassPlanet(GFX, name, { radius, etchCanvas, fieldCanvas })` builds one turning on its own, and `loadGlassPlanetMaps(name)` loads the canvases it is drawn from. The viewer's glass planets and the wizard staff's planet toppers both use it. |
| `props/metalglobe` | `metalglobe` | A planet in solid metal with its relief engraved into it, from a relief canvas with the height in its alpha (`loadEarthRelief`, `loadMarsEtch`, `loadMoonEtch`, `loadJupiterEtch({ relief: true })`). `createMetalGlobe(GFX, { radius, relief, metal, height, bump, soften, segments })`; `setMetal(name)` takes any of `METALS` (steel, silver, gold, copper, bronze, brass, titanium, chrome, platinum, rose gold, iron, pewter); `orient(lat, lon)`, `update(dt)`. `studioEnvironment(GFX, renderer)` makes a bright studio for it to reflect. |
| `props/resinglobe` | `resinglobe` | A planet in cast resin, the dice's material (glossy, clearcoated), its relief engraved into it: `createResinGlobe(GFX, { radius, relief, color })`, or `colors: { low, high }` to color the engraved relief apart from the rest (the Earth's green land on its blue sea). |
| `props/coin` | `coin` | A coin of the repository's logo, raised on both faces (cut into the geometry from `textures/coin/logo`, white on black), with a raised rim, in any of `METALS` (`props/metalglobe`): `createCoin(GFX, { radius, logo, metal })`; `setMetal(name)`, `update(dt)`. Stands on its edge and turns about the vertical. |

## heroes

The balls the games are played as, each with what it is made of.

| Path | Versions (games) | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `heroes/tater` | `tater` (debater) | The Tater: a potato with a debater's opinions, rough-skinned, stepping about the pan (`createPotato({ GFX })`). |
| `heroes/debater-egg` | `debater-egg` (debater) | The Egg: Marc, smooth and speckled, rocking and rolling (`createEgg({ GFX })`). The metal version (`createMetalEgg({ GFX, metal })`) uses all 12 shared finishes and supports `setMetal(name)`. The clear-glass version (`createGlassEgg({ GFX, mist })`) uses the engine's transmissive glass and optionally carries animated white mist with a restrained warm-yellow centre; `setMist(show)` toggles it. The wooden version (`createWoodEgg({ GFX, species, finish })`) is turned from any species and finish of `textures/wood`, the grain running tip to tip, and `setWood(species, finish)` changes either. The chocolate version (`createChocolateEgg({ GFX, chocolate })`) is molded `milk`, `dark` or `white` chocolate (`textures/chocolate`), glossy, with the seam where the mold met; `setChocolate(kind)` changes it. `createEgg({ GFX, appearance, ... })` makes any of `EGG_APPEARANCES` from one set of options, and `reach` sets how far it rolls from where it stands. All reuse the same Egg shape and movement. |
| `heroes/alan` | `alan` (alan) | Alan's eye: a sphere of clear glass with an iris painted deep inside it, the marble's original (`createEye(GFX)`), its attention, hung in its sky (`textures/skies/cloudsea`). |
| `heroes/blubber` | `blubber` (blubber) | Blubber, the Blueberry avatar: a squashed deep-blue berry with a waxy bloom over a glowing juice core, five dried sepals in its crown, a rim glow and two halos, its skin moving in lobes of waves and its palette drifting (`createBlubber(GFX, { size })`; `update(dt)` each frame, `setMode` for idle, listening, thinking, speaking). |
| `heroes/vibey` | `vibey` (vibey) | Vibey: a glowing five-pointed slime star that swells, spins and pulses with its mood (`createStar({ stage, GFX })`; `standIn` gives it a stage anywhere). Its liquid-metal variant (`createMetalStar({ stage, GFX, metal })`) keeps the same shape, movement, moods and grabbing, with all 12 finishes from `props/metalglobe` and a live `setMetal(name)`. |
| `heroes/slimey` | `slimey` (slimey) | Slimey: a glassy green orb of slime that deforms in lobes as it talks (`createSlimeOrb({ stage, GFX })`). Its liquid-metal variant (`createMetalSlimeOrb({ stage, GFX, metal })`) reuses the orb, core, bubbles, deformation and state controls with all 12 finishes from `props/metalglobe` and a live `setMetal(name)`. Its lava variant (`createLavaSlimeOrb({ stage, GFX })`) replaces the slime shell, core, glow and bubbles with a continuous animated basalt-and-magma surface. Its molten-glass variant (`createMoltenSlimeOrb({ stage, GFX })`) keeps the same lobes and moods in hot orange-red glass, with a procedural swirl of deep red, orange and white-hot yellow painted onto the shell (`paintMoltenSwirl`, seamless on the sphere) and its heat rising with its energy; no mist and no bubbles. |
| `heroes/krystal` | `krystal` (krystal) | Krystal, an animated prop: a crystal ball on a gold stand, a cloud of colour turning and churning inside it (`createKrystal({ stage, GFX })`). |
| `heroes/standin` | `standin` | A stand-in for the stage the avatar apps were written for, so Vibey, Slimey and Krystal stand anywhere. |
| `heroes/die` | `die` (dungeon-roller) | The party rolls through the dungeon as Nat's d20 (`nat/geometry.js`): the same purple resin, the same inked edges, the same numbers, scaled down to a little under a tile across. |
| `heroes/hamster` | `hamster` (petroll) | The player, made the way the marble in Madness is: two parts. |
| `heroes/mace` | `mace` (metroll, metrlol) | Metroll. |
| `heroes/marble` | `marble` (madness) | The marble is Alan's eye (`alan/src/client/eye/model.js`): the same sphere of clear glass — a transmissive physical material, index 1.5, all but perfectly smooth, with a clearcoat — shrunk to a mar… |
| `heroes/morningstar` | `morningstar` (metroll, metrlol) | The head of a morning star: a ball of dark forged steel with square spikes set into it, the kind on the end of a chain in a museum. |
| `heroes/nat/geometry` | `geometry` (dungeon-roller) | Nat's d20, copied from `nat/src/client/nat/geometry.js`. |
| `heroes/rock` | `rock` (rocknroller, rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii, metroll) | Rock. |
| `heroes/rock-jewel` | `createJewelRock`, `createJewelBoulder`, `JEWELS` (engine) | The granite stone's shape, cut from a translucent gem instead: clear glass tinted by its color, the granite's grain sampled in 3D as inclusions, with no picture laid on it, and a mist of the same color inside. Ten colors (`JEWEL_CHOICES`: sapphire, ruby, emerald, amber, amethyst, topaz, aquamarine, garnet, peridot, tourmaline), or any hex as `color`; `setColour()` and `setMist()`. |
| `heroes/yarn/ball` | `ball` (catroller) | As the tube in `model.js`: sides round it, and ply phase per metre over the texture's tile. |
| `heroes/yarn/model` | `model` (catroller) | Carol's body: the wound ball and the strand laid out behind it, as two tubes built once, and `pose(s)` — everything about how she looks follows from how far along the floor she has rolled. |
| `heroes/yarn/path` | `path` (catroller) | Where the ball rolls: a gentle S on the diagonal, from the back of the room on the left toward the front on the right of the camera's usual seat — she comes forward to talk, and goes back when it i… |
| `heroes/yarn/winding` | `winding` (catroller) | The ball, wound: one continuous strand, laid turn by turn round a hollow the size of two fingers, the way a hand winds a ball, until its surface averages `R_TARGET`. |

## scenery

The world round the ball: the town's street furniture and vehicles (`bakeData` in models/legacy-bake), the dungeon's walls, torches and exit, and the light show that lights a venue (`lightshow`: createLightshow(GFX, venue)).

| Path | Versions (games) | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `scenery/civic` | `civic` (metrlol) | The machinery of the city, sculpted (same conventions as `street.js`): the charging posts on the Brussels forecourt, the rubber stamps of the stamping hall (their gantry standing still, the stamp i… |
| `scenery/discourse` | `discourse` (metrlol) | What there is to find in the discourse, sculpted the same way as the rest (see `street.js`): the whetstone stand (Metroll's whetstone on a bench, where the spikes get sharpened back and the ball is… |
| `scenery/dungeon` | `dungeon` (dungeon-roller) | The dungeon as it is drawn: flagstone floors, brick walls falling away into the dark, the lava (lava.js), torches with live flames, and the stairs down — a ring of runes on the floor under a stone … |
| `scenery/ice` | `ice` (blubber) | The Ice Cube avatar, as it is, brought onto this engine: the same rounded block (a sphere pulled out to a superellipsoid, edges as sharp as its mood says), the same frozen-in facets, the same dished top, the same clear ice with its frost rim, cloudy core … |
| `scenery/maze` | `maze` (blubber) | The mazes. |
| `scenery/mazepieces` | `mazepieces` (blubber) | The pieces a maze night is dressed in: the candles and lamps on its walls, with live flames, and the moon gate out — a stone arch with a crescent over it and a swirl in it that wakes when every lantern is lit. |
| `scenery/lightshow` | `lightshow` (metroll)<br>`lightshow.rocknroller-ii` (rocknroller-ii)<br>`lightshow.rocknroller-iii` (rocknroller-iii)<br>`lightshow.rocknroller` (rocknroller) | The light show. |
| `scenery/odds` | `odds` (petroll) | Odds and ends for the jobs and for knocking flying: lawn flamingos, yard signs, crates, survey flags, and the things a job has the hamster carry (a jar of pickled eggs, dynamite, a film reel). |
| `scenery/oil` | `oil` (petroll) | The gas station's and the oil field's machinery, sculpted: the pumps and the air pump, the pumpjack (its frame standing still, its walking beam and horsehead nodding), oil drums, a wellhead, a flar… |
| `scenery/street` | `street` (petroll)<br>`street.metrlol` (metrlol) | The furniture of the streets and yards, sculpted. |
| `scenery/vehicles` | `vehicles` (petroll)<br>`vehicles.metrlol` (metrlol) | The traffic, sculpted: a sedan, a hatchback, a pickup, a box truck, a tanker, and a rusted-out junker for the yard. |

## textures

Painted on canvases at startup. `painters` is the toolkit and the floors and walls; `venue` the rock clubs' floors, walls, belts, grilles, tape, shutters, panels and glows; `town/` the town's; `lava` a material; `rooms/` what shiny things reflect (each `paintRoom`) and `skies/` what is round the scene (each `paintSky`).

| Path | Versions (games) | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `textures/road` | (engine) | Asphalt and concrete, painted as what they are made of, to the granite's standard: `asphaltTexture(GFX, { age, cracks, patches, stains, seed })` is crushed stone in a bitumen binder (every stone its own angular, faceted grain of granite, diorite, limestone, feldspar, quartz or basalt, three sizes of them with the contact shadow each throws, sand and pits between, the binder worn off the stones a worn road shows and coating them on a fresh one, hairline cracks, tar bands laid over them and oil), and `concreteTexture(GFX, { finish: 'broom' \| 'trowel' \| 'aged', slabs, wear, cracks, stains, seed })` is cement paste with its sand, bugholes, exposed pebbles, a broom's ridges, a control joint round each slab with years of dirt in it, and hairline cracks. Each gives `{ map, bump }`, wrapping and seamless, 2048 pixels (a millimetre a pixel for asphalt) and `TILE` metres across; `paintAsphalt` and `paintConcrete` are the same as raw pixels with no canvas, so they run under node (`node scripts/preview-road.mjs <dir> asphalt` writes PNGs of them). |
| `textures/ground` | (engine) | Ground, painted to the same standard as `textures/road`: `turfTexture(GFX, { health, length, clover, dry, seed })` is grass as blades (every blade its own curved, tapering stroke, darker at the root, lighter at the tip, a pale rib down the middle, lit on the side facing the light, in four layers over thatch and soil, with clover leaves, dead straw, and with `dry` worn patches of soil with stones); `gravelTexture(GFX, { kind: 'ballast' \| 'roof' \| 'path', seed })` is stones laid on stones in three sizes (angular crushed railway ballast, rounded roof gravel over tar, pea gravel) with the shadow each throws; `paversTexture(GFX, { kind: 'brick' \| 'grey' \| 'tan', wear, seed })` is fired bricks in a running bond, each its own colour and speckle with kiln flash, bevel and the odd chip, in sand joints with dirt and moss. Each gives `{ map, bump }`, wrapping, 2048 pixels and `TILE.<name>` metres across; `paintTurf`, `paintGravel` and `paintPavers` are the raw pixels with no canvas, for node. |
| `textures/roofing` | (engine) | Roofs, painted the same way: `shinglesTexture(GFX, { color: 'charcoal' \| 'brown' \| 'grey' \| 'green', age, seed })` is asphalt shingles in courses (each course shadowed at its top and lit at its foot, three tabs to a strip with the slots cut between, every tab a shade of its own, a scatter of granules, and with age streaks of dirt, weathering and moss), laid `u` along the eave and `v` up the slope; `membraneTexture(GFX, { tone: 'white' \| 'grey' \| 'black' \| 'tan', age, seed })` is a single-ply flat roof with welded seams, a screw plate along each, the ripples of the deck under it and dirt gathered in its ponds. `TILE.shingles` and `TILE.membrane` metres across; `paintShingles` and `paintMembrane` are the raw pixels, for node. |
| `textures/facades` | (engine) | Building facades painted from photographs of real ones, one storey of one bay (`TILE` 3.6 m square) to repeat up a wall: `facadeTexture(GFX, kind)` for `curtain` (a glass curtain wall: three panes a storey of blue-grey reflective glass with sky and cloud in them, silver mullions, a spandrel panel and the slab line), `precast` (cream precast concrete with formwork grain, punched windows in deep reveals with proud sills and a brown spandrel band), `terracotta` (a rain-screen of large reeded panels, each its own firing, with open shadow joints, round a tall blue-green glass bay in a silver frame) and `sandstone` (rough-faced red sandstone in uneven courses, pitted, with arched windows ringed by dressed voussoirs and a sill). `{ map, bump }`, wrapping; `paintFacade` is the raw pixels, for node. |
| `textures/kitchen` | `kitchen` (short-order) | The kitchen's surfaces, painted at load: `marbleTexture(GFX)` (honed Calacatta, veined with a gold bloom, tiling), `greenTileTexture(GFX)` (bottle-green glazed subway tile in dark grout, every tile its own depth of green) and `brushedTexture(GFX, size, base)` (brushed metal, for the brass). Each is a wrapping texture of its own, and `null` under node. |
| `textures/lava` | `lava` (dungeon-roller) | Lava Slimey's lava (`createLavaMaterial(GFX, { mapping })`): a dull basalt crust under an animated molten layer, whose glints give the melt its gloss. `createLavaFloorMaterial(GFX)` is the older floor shader, kept for compatibility. |
| `textures/lavapit` | `lavapit` (dungeon-roller; for Rock 'n' Roller and Metroll too) | The lava pit: Slimey's lava rolled out flat. The same melt (flows, colors, bubbling) computed per pixel in 3D world space in one pass, with procedural basalt, so there is no baked texture, UV stretching or visible seam. The melt is glossy, the basalt dull. Colour and size are configurable: `hue` (radians; 0 is lava, about 2.9 is an electrified blue floor), `scale` (default `SLIMEY_SCALE`, Slimey's own density, so a 3-unit pit shows about three Slimeys' worth; halve it for twice the size), `coverage` (how much is molten) and `glow`. `createLavaSurface(GFX, geometry, options)` is the lava alone for any pit geometry (`mesh`, `update(time)`); `createLavaPit(GFX, { width, depth, sink, ...options })` is a whole pit with stone rim, walls and a flickering light. The dungeon's lava uses it. |
| `textures/blubber` | `blubber` (blubber) | Every surface's texture, painted on a canvas at startup, as Dungeon Roller's stone is: a colour map near white (the tile's colour comes from the vertex colours under it) and a bump map that raises what stands out. |
| `textures/bog` | `bog` (blubber) | The bog: something green brewing in the witch's clearings and round the edge of her wood. |
| `textures/rooms/house` | `house` (catroller) | A room, as an equirectangular canvas: cream walls warm with lamplight, a dark window with the moon in it, a wooden floor. |
| `textures/rooms/parlour` | `parlour` (krystal) | The fortune teller's parlour, as Krystal's brass and glass see it: the night of `skies/cosmos` with a couple of warm lamps low in the dark and a violet glow off the cloth below. |
| `textures/rooms/softbox` | `softbox` (vibey, slimey) | A photographer's softbox room: pale above, grey to a dark floor, and two soft lights high up, one white and one cool blue. What Vibey's and Slimey's glossy skins reflect. |
| `textures/rooms/studio` | `studio` (madness) | The studio, as an equirectangular canvas: a dark room, lighter overhead, with a broad softbox above, a warm strip on one side and a cool one on the other. |
| `textures/rooms/town` | `town` (metrlol, petroll) | What the chrome, the paint and the puddles reflect: the night, and the sodium and neon of the town round them. |
| `textures/rooms/vault` | `vault` (dungeon-roller) | The vault, as an equirectangular canvas: dark stone all round, a little warm light low down from torches somewhere, a cold grey shaft from above. |
| `textures/rooms/venue` | `venue` (rocknroller, rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii, metroll) | The room the reflections come from, as an equirectangular canvas: a dark ceiling, the venue's colours in a ring of lights round the walls, and a bright rig overhead. The moods' rooms add strip lights overhead (`strips`). |
| `textures/skies/cloudsea` | `cloudsea` (alan) | Alan's night: stars over a sea of cloud seen from so high up the horizon has dropped below level, a few towns lit through the gaps, and the sun straight overhead. |
| `textures/earth/map` | `map` | The land as coordinates (`land.js`: Natural Earth 1:50m, thinned to 0.04°): `landRings()`, `landMask(w, h)`, `isLand(lat, lon)` and `createEtchCanvas()`, the frosted etching of the continents. |
| `textures/mars/map` | `map` | The actual surface of Mars, transcribed for glass: MOLA laser altimetry (Mars Global Surveyor, 32 px/degree) shaded as relief and stored as a 4096 × 2048 JPEG (`relief.js`, from `scripts/mars-relief.py`), and `loadMarsEtch()`, the frosted etching of it for `createGlassGlobe({ etchCanvas })`. `RADIUS_KM` and `SIZE_VS_EARTH` give its true size. |
| `textures/moon/map` | `map` | The actual surface of the Moon, transcribed for glass: LRO LOLA laser altimetry (LDEM_16, 16 px/degree) shaded as relief and stored as a 4096 × 2048 JPEG (`relief.js`, from `scripts/moon-relief.py`), and `loadMoonEtch()`, the frosted etching of it for `createGlassGlobe({ etchCanvas })`. `RADIUS_KM` and `SIZE_VS_EARTH` give its true size. |
| `textures/jupiter/map` | `loadJupiterMap()` | Jupiter's clouds as a 2:1 colour layout (`layout.js`, from `scripts/jupiter-map.py`, which projects one photograph of the disc onto the sphere; the far side is the mean of each latitude's belts), and `loadJupiterMap()`, a canvas of it for `createGlassGlobe(...).setField(canvas)`, where it drifts as mist. `RADIUS_KM` and `SIZE_VS_EARTH` give its true size. |
| `textures/skies/cosmos` | `cosmos` (krystal) | Krystal's night: deep indigo going to black overhead, drifts of nebula in violet, rose and teal, and stars, a handful with a glint of colour. |
| `textures/skies/embers` | `embers` (dungeon-roller) | The dark round the dungeon: black above, a faint ember-red haze far below. |
| `textures/skies/haze` | `haze` (madness) | The sky round the scene: a deep blue haze at the horizon, dark above and below. |
| `textures/skies/horizons` | `horizons` (metroll) | The sky round each track, painted on a canvas: a gradient from `sky`, stars if it is night, and along the horizon (`horizon`, in `skyline`'s colour, with a `glow` of its own colour where the place … |
| `textures/skies/night` | `night` (catroller) | Outside the house: night, deep blue above, a little warmer toward the bottom. |
| `textures/skies/skyline` | `skyline` (rocknroller, rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii) | The sky round the stop, painted on a canvas: a gradient from `sky`, stars if it is night, and along the horizon (`horizon`, in `skyline`'s colour): rolling `hills` with a town's lights on them, a `… A venue's dark (`cloudy: false`) has no clouds. |
| `textures/skies/town` | `town` (petroll, metrlol) | The night over Petroleum Springs, as an equirectangular canvas: stars, a moon, a sky going to a dirty orange at the horizon where the refineries light it from below, and on the horizon the silhouet… Metrlol's horizon (`on: 'city'`) has a city's towers, data centres and wind turbines instead. |
| `textures/town/paint` | `paint` (metrlol, petroll) | From Rock 'n' Roller III, with Petroleum Springs's own added at the end (lawn, paving slabs, shingles, tar paper, pool tiles, kerbs). |
| `textures/town/surfaces` | `surfaces` (petroll, metrlol) | What the ground is made of, tile by tile: how it looks — `tex`, the floor texture painted for it (`paint.js`), tinted `top`; `wtex` and `wall` for the sides where it stands above its neighbour — an… |
| `textures/town/textures` | `textures` (petroll, metrlol) | The materials the ground and the walls are drawn with: each surface's floor texture (`paint.js`) and its bump, the colour and the night's light in the vertex colours, and how it shines — oil and pu… |
| `textures/venue` | `venue` (metroll, rocknroller, rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii) | Every texture, painted on a canvas at startup: the floors and walls of the sets (concrete, planks, lino, carpet, diamond plate, grass, wet asphalt, dirt, grating, cobbles; plywood, foam, brick pape… Each game's poster names and shutter stencil are set with `bill()`. |

## music

Made on the spot with Web Audio. `band` is a whole band with its songs (`THEMES`), `theory` its scales, forms and effects; `score` a smaller orchestra with its own themes.

| Path | Versions (games) | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `music/band` | `band` (metroll, metrlol)<br>`band.rocknroller-ii` (rocknroller-ii)<br>`band.rocknroller-iii` (rocknroller-iii)<br>`band.rocknroller` (rocknroller) | The compilation's music. |
| `music/score` | `score` (catroller)<br>`score.dungeon-roller` (dungeon-roller) | The music: a sneaky little jazz trio played live with Web Audio, no samples — a plucked upright bass walking on every beat, brushes on the snare and a ride ticking over the top, vibraphone chords, … |

## moods

The look of every set: its light, its sky and what its chrome reflects (each with its painter), the film it is shot on (the grade on the picture, the grain and the vignette over it, and the interface on the same stock where the game does that), its weather, and its band, theme and tempo; and the set's own `look` and `palette`. `stage.setMood(mood)` dresses a stage in one; `MOODS` (`moods/index`) has them all.

|---|---|---|

## Stage gear

The rock'n'roll games' venues, dressed and rigged, in `scenery/gear/` (Rock 'n' Roller I, II and III and Metroll use them; the asset viewer lists every one under Stage gear). Each game's own copies are merged here: one version of each.

| File | Games | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `scenery/gear/decor` | rocknroller, rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii, metroll | The props over a venue's tiles (`PROPS`): amps, road cases, drums, speakers, the bar, a pool table, a jukebox, pinball, kegs, tables, with the furniture, dressing and sights below; `createProps(GFX, venue)` builds a venue's, each facing the open floor (`FACING`, `openSide`). |
| `scenery/gear/furniture` | rocknroller, rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii, metroll | A mixing desk, racks of gear, arena seats, pianos, hay bales, portable loos, tents, racking, a dome, crowd barriers, the stands. |
| `scenery/gear/dressing` | rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii, metroll | The film sets' and the tour's dressing: airbags, barrels, bookcases, cameras, a cannon, chests, coffins, a craft table, crates, desks, lamps, mirrors, a sedan, statues, tombstones... |
| `scenery/gear/sights` | rocknroller-iii, metroll | The places' own furniture: the world tour's (`tour`: a phone box, a café, a well, a ski rack...) and the compilation's (`compilation`: an anvil, a furnace, a pink limo, a hot tub, tombs...). |
| `scenery/gear/machinery` | rocknroller, rocknroller-ii, rocknroller-iii, metroll | What moves or is taken: drops that come down on the beat (a speaker stack, sandbags, a rig, a boulder, a piston, a chandelier, a crate), bursts out of the floor, lifts, gates, breakaway panels, bumpers (a pinball post and the rest) and pickups. A game hands over its pickups with `usePickups`. |
| `scenery/gear/travel` | rocknroller-iii, metroll | The tracks' drops, rides, bumpers and bursts (`DROPS`, `RIDES`, `BUMPERS`, `BURSTS`), the world tour's and the compilation's together. |
